# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Games

## I. PLACEMENT GAMES
Games where you place objects, numbers, or marks in cells

### A. Light/Illumination
- **Akari** - Place light bulbs that illuminate rows/columns

### B. Number Placement
- **Sudoku** - Place numbers 1-9 in rows, columns, and blocks
- **Nansuke** - Fill blank cells with numbers from a list
- **Makaro** - Fill cells with numbers based on room constraints and arrow directions
- **Ripple Effect** - Fill cells with consecutive numbers in rooms
- **Kurotto** - Color cells based on number constraints in circles

### C. Shape/Block Placement
- **Shikaku** - Divide grid into rectangles containing one number
- **Fillomino** - Fill blocks with numbers matching block size
- **LITS** - Place tetrominoes in regions
- **Evolomino** - Place squares on arrows with progressive growth
- **Shakashaka** - Place triangles in squares to form rectangles
- **Sashigane** - Divide grid into L-shaped blocks

### D. Coloring/Shading
- **Hitori** - Color cells to eliminate duplicate numbers
- **Kurodoko** - Color cells black based on number constraints
- **Nurikabe** - Color cells black to form walls around white regions
- **Nurimisaki** - Color cells black with white "promontories"
- **Nuritwin** - Shade cells in pairs within regions
- **Sto-stone** - Color cells that "drop" to fill bottom half
- **Usowan** - Color cells based on neighbor count (with one wrong number per region)
- **Tilepaint** - Color tiles based on diagonal number constraints
- **Norinori** - Color cells in pairs within regions
- **Heyawake** - Color cells with constraints on white cell continuity

### E. Block/Region Definition
- **Chained Block** - Define black cell blocks with size constraints
- **Double Choco** - Divide grid into blocks with matching white/gray pairs
- **Five Cells** - Divide grid into five-cell blocks with line constraints

## II. LINE-DRAWING GAMES
Games where you draw continuous lines or loops

### A. Single Loop Games
- **Masyu** - Loop through white and black circles with turn constraints
- **Slitherlink** - Connect dots to form loop with number constraints
- **Dotchi-Loop** - Loop through white circles with turn constraints in regions
- **Mid-loop** - Loop with black circles as midpoints of line segments
- **Moon-or-Sun** - Loop through rooms alternating between moon/sun cells
- **Nagareru** - Loop following arrow directions with wind constraints
- **Suraromu** - Loop starting/ending at numbered circle, passing gates
- **Yajilin** - Loop avoiding black cells indicated by arrows

### B. Path/Connection Games
- **Numberlink** - Connect pairs of same numbers with non-crossing lines
- **Hashiwokakero** - Connect islands with bridges (up to 2 per pair)
- **Pencils** - Draw lines from pencil tips with length constraints

## III. MOVEMENT GAMES
Games where you move objects to new positions

- **Satogaeri** - Move circles to countries based on distance numbers
- **Yosenabe** - Move circles into gray areas with sum constraints

## IV. FILLING GAMES
Games where you fill cells with specific marks or patterns

### A. Mark-Based
- **Juosan** - Fill cells with horizontal/vertical marks with territory constraints

### B. Maze/Path Creation
- **Nurimeizu** - Paint cells to create maze from S to G

## V. HYBRID/COMPLEX GAMES
Games combining multiple mechanics

- **Hebi** - Place sequential numbers (1-5) forming snakes with visibility constraints
- **Choco Banana** - (Rules incomplete in document)

---

## Alternative Organization by Primary Mechanic

| **Mechanic** | **Games** |
|---|---|
| **Placement** | Akari, Sudoku, Nansuke, Makaro, Ripple Effect, Kurotto, Shikaku, Fillomino, LITS, Evolomino, Shakashaka, Sashigane |
| **Coloring** | Hitori, Kurodoko, Nurikabe, Nurimisaki, Nuritwin, Sto-stone, Usowan, Tilepaint, Norinori, Heyawake, Chained Block, Double Choco, Five Cells |
| **Looping** | Masyu, Slitherlink, Dotchi-Loop, Mid-loop, Moon-or-Sun, Nagareru, Suraromu, Yajilin |
| **Connecting** | Numberlink, Hashiwokakero, Pencils |
| **Moving** | Satogaeri, Yosenabe |
| **Marking** | Juosan |
| **Pathfinding** | Nurimeizu |
| **Sequential** | Hebi |
